Case B - Diagonal ramps (plan view, whole sheet): A four-leg intersection plan shown with a two-way street running left to right across the middle of the sheet and a cross street running vertically on the left. Each corner has a diagonal curb ramp (labeled DIAGONAL CURB RAMP) with a detectable warning surface at the corner. A crosswalk made of heavy transverse bars crosses the main street at the left, with its limits marked by two dashed vertical lines. The dashed line on the left is labeled CURB LINE PROLONGATION. A pedestrian crossing island sits in the center median of the main street, with a left-turn arrow shown in the adjacent lane. The island has an approach nose at the left (the end facing the crosswalk) and a wider body at the right. The same island is drawn twice, once at the top in the main view and again at the bottom as an option.

Main view, crossing island: The island is drawn as a rounded rectangle with the detectable warning surfaces shown as stippled strips on both sides of a cut-through path, which carries a 2% MAX cross slope arrow. The approach nose at the left end is labeled APPROACH NOSE, DESIGN FOR SITE CONDITIONS, SEE NOTE 5, and measures 2' MIN in the direction of travel, with its edge aligned with the base of the diagonal curb ramps (callout ALIGN EDGE WITH BASE OF DIAGONAL CURB RAMPS). The main island body is 8' MIN long. A vertical dimension on the island is labeled 6' MIN, SEE NOTE 6, and the cut-through between the nose and the island is labeled DETECTABLE WARNING SURFACE - SEE NOTE 4 and MATCH CROSSWALK WIDTH WHERE POSSIBLE (SEE NOTE 5). Each island segment carries R4-7 and OM1-1 signs (TYP) and RPMs (raised pavement markers, TYP, SEE NOTE 9). The TOTAL CROSSING, SEE NOTE 10, is dimensioned from the curb line prolongation across the full crosswalk width to the far end of the island body.

Striping at the island: Beyond the island nose a 4" SOLID YELLOW LINE 1' OFF CENTER MEDIAN runs along both edges of the double yellow median. Between those lines a series of 12" SOLID YELLOW LINE diagonals SPACED 20' C-C fills the approach and departure area of the island, sloping across the roadway.

Option when island is less than 6' wide (SEE NOTE 3): A second, smaller copy of the layout shown at the bottom of the sheet. The island body is labeled LESS THAN 6' in width, and a separate vertical dimension on the striped area to its right is labeled 4' MIN, SEE NOTE 6. The 2' MIN approach nose, the 8' MIN island length, the TOTAL CROSSING (SEE NOTE 10) dimension, MATCH CROSSWALK WIDTH WHERE POSSIBLE (SEE NOTE 5), the R4-7 and OM1-1 signs and the 12" diagonal yellow lines are repeated as in the main view. The view title is CASE B - DIAGONAL RAMPS (upper right) and OPTION WHEN ISLAND IS LESS THAN 6' WIDE (bottom).

Document page: A page of the City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP). The header reads Subject: Application for Striping, Channelization, & Special Signing, Section 531, Date 05-20, Page 15. There is no drawing title block and no drawing is shown.

Lead-in paragraph: The top of the page carries the end of a paragraph (it begins on the previous page) saying that specifications and guidelines for these signs are shown in S-502.0, that the Department will allow these signs to be posted in accordance with S-502.0 and a Street Use Permit, and that due to their unique nature and the multitude of designs the Department will not inventory nor maintain them.

Table 1, Application of Striping and Pavement Markings: three columns (Striping/Marking Component, Application, Reference to California MUTCD), ten rows.
Row 1: Skip Centerline | Allows passing of opposing traffic on two lane streets. | Figure 3A-101 (CA), Detail 1 and Figure 3B-1, a
Row 2: Partial Passing Centerline | Allows passing of opposing traffic generally on two-lane streets from one direction only. | Figure 3A-103 (CA), Detail 15 and Figure 3B-3, a
Row 3: Double Yellow Centerline | Prohibits passing of opposing traffic, but allows crossing. | Figure 3A-104 (CA), Detail 21 and Figure 3B-2, a
Row 4: Striped Median | Striping that separates opposing traffic flows and prohibits passing and crossing. Internal separation must be at least two feet for enforcement. | Figure 3A-107 (CA), Detail 28 and Figure 3B-4
Row 5: Two-Way Left-Turn Lane (2WLTL) | Provides midblock left-turn storage. May be used at non-signalized intersections to provide storage for both intersectional left turns and nearby driveways from the other direction. | Figure 3A-108 (CA), Detail 31 and Figure 3B-7 (CA)
Row 6: Left Edge Line | Delineates the left edge of roadway or median and is parallel to the edge of roadway. | Figure 3A-105 (CA), Detail 24
Row 7: Left Channelization Line | Delineates left edge of travel path where it is not parallel to the edge of roadway. | Figure 3A-104 (CA), Detail 21
Row 8: Cigar Nose | Delineates a tapered striped median at "T" intersection crossings. It is commonly used where the left-turn radius from the stem roadway of the "T" is less than 70 feet or where it is not necessary to provide left-turn storage into driveways near the top of the "T" via a 2WLTL. | Figure 3B-2, b
Row 9: Reversal | Identifies and provides the reverse curve travel path into a unidirectional left-turn lane or a 2WLTL. | Figure 3B-2, b
Row 10: Left Edge Cross Hatch | Provides emphasis in striped medians or between the left edge of roadway and Left Channelization Line or Left Edge Line, at least 5 feet in width. Also, it clarifies that the area is not part of the traveled way. Is aligned at 45 degrees diagonally forward with respect to the direction of travel. | Figures 3B-5

description:
Document page: A page of the City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation Manual of Policies and Procedures (MPP). The header reads Subject: Application for Striping, Channelization, & Special Signing, Section 531, Date 05-20, Page 16. There is no drawing title block and no drawing is shown. The sheet is a continuation of Table 1 from the previous page.

Table 1 - Application of Striping and Pavement Markings (Cont'd): a table with the same three columns as the previous page (component, application, reference to California MUTCD). This page has no column header row, only the continued title row, and twelve rows.
Row 1: Reversible Lane Marking | Delineates a lane that is reversed in directional flow during various times of the day. | Figure 3B-6
Row 2: Lane Line | Separates concurrent through lanes. | Figure 3A-102 (CA), Detail 8
Row 3: Barrier Line | Separates turn lanes from through lanes or other turn lanes. | Figure 3A-112 (CA), Detail 38A
Row 4: Right Edge Line | Delineates the right edge of roadway and is parallel to the edge of roadway. | Figure 3A-106 (CA), Detail 27B
Row 5: Right Channelization Line | Delineates right edge of travel path where it is not parallel to the edge or roadway. | Figure 3A-112 (CA), Detail 38A
Row 6: Striped Island | Physically separates converging or diverging traffic flows and prohibits vehicular crossing. Internal separation must be at least 2 feet for enforcement. | Figure 3B-8 (CA), 3B-9 (CA), 3B-12 and 3B-15
Row 7: Lane Drop Line or "Elephant Track" | Transition striping for an entrapped-turn lane or an advance turn lane. See S-491.0. | Figure 3A-111 (CA), Detail 37B and Figure 3B-11 (CA)
Row 8: Bike Lane Line | Separates the travel path between bicycles and motor vehicles. The Bike Lane Line is broken at least 96' upstream of the intersection in order to identify where right turning motor vehicles may cross the bicycle lane. | Figure 3A-112 (CA) Details 39 and 39A, and Figure 9C-6
Row 9: Right Edge Cross-Hatch | Provides emphasis in striped islands or between the right edge of roadway and Right Channelization Line or Right Edge Line, at least 5-feet in width. Also, it clarifies that the area is not part of the traveled way. Is aligned at 45 degrees diagonally forward with respect to the direction of travel. See S-444.0 and 485.0 | (Not Shown)
Row 10: Chevron | Provides emphasis within a striped island or a gore area at least 5 feet in width where concurrent traffic travels on either side. See S-493.0, Sheets 5 and 6 of 7. | Figure 3B-12 and 3B-15, c
Row 11: Hook (Wrap) and Bar | Used at the downstream end of a Barrier Line for a Trap Turn Lane, where the adjacent lane is a through lane. Where the adjacent lane is a concurrent turn lane the Bar is not used. See S-491.0 and S-405.0. | Figure 3B-13, d
Row 12: Crosswalk (Marked) | Emphasizes the legal crosswalk at signalized intersections, indicates a preferred legal crosswalk at non-signalized intersections, and identifies a legal marked crosswalk where no legal unmarked crosswalk exists. Parallel lines, 12" wide generally are 15 feet or 10 feet apart, with minimum width of 10 feet. See S-490.0 and S-493.0. | Figure 3B-17
